properties.name: Stored data is rechecked against the current schema: a refused_by_schema detector by the write rule itself, and a gate that each narrowing ships its migration
properties.rationale:
THE CAUSE (fact:root-cause-a-schema-narrowing-ships-its-migration-by-hand-per-pair-and-nothing-rechecks-a-store-2026-10-02, VS Code --call field report limitation 18), confirmed on main c4e1cbd before the fix: Schema::validate_edge had one store caller, StorageEngine::create_edge; export_graph, opening a store and detect_defects never re-judged stored data; each narrowing carried its own migration for the pairs its census saw (REALIZES onto a Verification, rewritten in two hand-written copies, import and open). The failing-first test (a_stored_item_the_schema_now_refuses_is_reported.rs) failed in 8 of 10 cases on the unfixed code: every narrowed stored item reported zero.

THE CLASS, NOT THE PAIR: (1) the recheck asks THE SAME FUNCTIONS the write point refuses with — Schema::node_refusals / edge_refusals, which validate_node and the new validate_edge_write now refuse with the first of — after the import's own preparation, so it reports exactly what the import would refuse; a test holds the two to the same items. (2) The gate makes every future narrowing state its migration before it ships, against the LAST RELEASE (what reaches a consumer), and the entries are checked to do what they say. Its first run found the VERIFIES narrowing of 2026-08-08 refusing eight targets naming nothing (fact:the-verifies-narrowing-refused-eight-targets-naming-nothing-2026-10-03), repaired here.

MEASURED on this branch: main's own export (6,449 nodes, 41,817 edges) — refused_by_schema 0, examined 48,266; the schema rule over all of it costs ~120 ms of a 4.4 s in-memory release sweep. Triage C's legacy export (REALIZES and VERIFIES onto a Decision), loaded into a RocksDB store under the pre-narrowing endpoints: the binary's detect_defects names both with DOCUMENTS and GOVERNED_BY, and its --import refuses exactly those two.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: a warning on every export_graph (rejected in the decision as noise); a rewrite table for stored VALUES (no narrowing needs one yet — entry_problems refuses a value entry claiming Rewritten until one exists); treating a newly declared OPTIONAL property as a narrowing (bound stated in narrowing.rs). Enum-value removals on a stamped RocksDB store meet the provenance guard's open refusal first; NARROWINGS is now the registry of removed values that guard's comment asks for, and wiring its message to it is left open.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: detect_defects reports every stored node and edge the current schema refuses (refused_by_schema, critical), by the store's own write rule after the import's preparation, with the rule and the replacement the import names; propose_heal drafts the replacement and applies nothing. A test diffs the schema against the last release's acceptance snapshot and fails on any narrowing narrowing::NARROWINGS does not name with its migration. EDGE_REWRITES is the one table the import, every open and the recheck read; the provenance guard's retired types come from NARROWINGS; a refused VERIFIES now names what the check is evidence for.
